أَشْنَقُ Long; applied to a neck. (M.) And, as also ↓ مَشْنُوقٌ , Long in the head; applied to a horse and to a camel; and so شَنْقَآءُ [the fem. of the former] and ↓ شِنَاقٌ applied to the female. (M.) For the fem., see also شِنَاقٌ. ＝
-A2- [The fem.] شَنْقَآءُ signifies [also] A female bird that feeds her young ones with her bill, ejecting the food into their mouths. (O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
